Preflyt is a self-hosted shift-left engineering platform for software teams. It brings engineering standards, branch policies, CI validation and optional AI code reviews into your GitHub delivery workflow. Quick StartSelf-host Preflyt

CI pipelines and scanners produce results, but results alone do not establish whether a change meets your team's requirements. Checks can be missing, apply to a different revision, or vary across repositories and branches. Preflyt gives teams a consistent way to define engineering standards, apply branch-specific policies, verify CI evidence and review issues before release. Developers receive feedback on pull requests; engineering and platform teams gain visibility into unmet requirements and the evidence behind each decision. You run Preflyt on your own infrastructure with Docker Compose or the Kubernetes application bundle. A GitHub App connects the repositories you select. Your GitHub Actions workflows run the tests and scanners; optional AI reviews use the models and review instructions your organization chooses.

Repository profiles: languages, frameworks, CI, tests, lockfiles, containers, infrastructure as code and scanner configuration, each backed by file evidence at an exact commit. Engineering standards: five versioned packs (Baseline Engineering, Application Security, Backend Services, Frontend Applications and Infrastructure as Code) with recommendations based on your stack. Commit assessments: freeze the standards you selected and the CI results GitHub reported for a commit, so you can compare repositories and revisions over time. CI evidence: signed GitHub pull request, check and workflow events, plus bounded JUnit and SARIF reports submitted automatically by the Action. Contributors: who works on which repositories, from pull request and commit activity. AI review skills: optional, advisory reviews you configure per organization. AI never decides a result. Access control: GitHub or OIDC sign-in, organizations, teams and eight built-in roles. Notifications: an in-app inbox and email channels for assessment outcomes.

Select repositories, review recommended standards, publish a policy for the target branch, and add the Preflyt Action to your workflow. Preflyt evaluates the resulting evidence and publishes Preflyt / Engineering Readiness on the pull request. Development and main can have different requirements. You can begin with inspection and assessments, then enable PR checks and optional merge protection. GitHub blocks merges only when its rules require the check. AI feedback remains advisory and cannot waive a required engineering check. See How Preflyt works for the complete workflow and Getting Started to set up your first repository.

How Preflyt works, Evidence and trust and Status labels.
Preflyt is under active development. When a capability is not implemented yet, its page says so.
Preflyt is careful about what a piece of evidence actually proves. This page explains the levels, because they decide how to read every status in the app.

Kind Where it comes from What it proves Configuration Files in the repository at an exact commit That a supported setup exists, for example a workflow that mentions a scanner. Not that it ran. Reported CI result A signed GitHub webhook for a check or workflow run That GitHub reported this outcome for this commit. Not which rule it covered or which tool ran. Verified evidence An Action submission authenticated by GitHub OIDC, bound to report digests and verified GitHub workflow/job execution, or a verified native execution receipt That the configured checks produced usable evidence for the exact commit and policy. Report coverage and freshness still matter.

A job named "test" that succeeded does not tell Preflyt that your required tests ran. So: Preflyt never turns a provider success into a pass on its own. If you associate a CI result with a control by hand, it is stored as unverified and labelled Source not verified. A policy with no required checks is not evaluated, never an empty pass. Missing mandatory evidence is incomplete. For the normal Action flow, Preflyt verifies the repository, workflow, run attempt, PR head commit and completed jobs through GitHub, and binds the submitted report digests to that execution. The first verified run registers the workflow connection. Additional report signatures are optional; private repositories do not need a separate signer. Follow Pull request checks.
documents.s: Why a green job is not a pass

documents.t: Preflyt keeps results honest over time: A result with a missing timestamp does not inherit "just now". Expired and future-dated results never appear fresh. A newer result for the same source marks the older one as superseded (Newer result available). Two conflicting results with the same or unknown time are ambiguous (Multiple matching results). A snapshot is historical. It says nothing about the current state of a branch.

The Action submits bounded JUnit and SARIF reports from your workflow automatically. Preflyt stores summaries and checksums, not uploaded report bytes, CI logs or credentials. There is no manual report-import workflow in the UI. Older unverified records can remain in history; they do not become verified by being displayed in an assessment.
AI review is optional, per organization and advisory. It can explain or flag, but it never decides a quality gate result. The app keeps AI output separate from observed evidence.

Running scanners inside Preflyt is a separate, disabled-by-default capability. It needs its own controller, a signed independent isolation review, and reviewed tool images. Generated test fixtures do not establish production acceptance. Production acceptance is incomplete. Use GitHub Actions for normal onboarding; see Native execution for the implemented controls, current coverage and operator prerequisites.

Problems found in QA or production cost more than problems found while you design, code or review. Preflyt helps you catch them earlier, at your repository and your pull requests, by answering three questions at an exact commit: Which engineering checks apply to this repository? What evidence exists for each of them, and can you trust it? Is it ready to progress, or where are the gaps? Preflyt coordinates the scanners, tests and CI you already have. It is not a coding agent, an IDE, a replacement CI system or a code generator.

Step What Preflyt does Status Discover Profiles each selected repository with file evidence. Available Assess Freezes your standards and reported CI results at a commit. Available Validate Verifies where evidence came from, through authenticated submissions and verified GitHub execution, or reviewed native execution receipts. Available, see Evidence and trust Enforce Shows a merge review result for every report. A published policy publishes a Preflyt / Engineering Readiness check on each pull request. Merge Protection can require it through GitHub rulesets. Observe by default; enforcement is opt-in Improve Trends, contributor activity and advisory AI review. Available

Validation: discovers repository context and normalises CI evidence. Governance: holds your standards, requirements and quality gates. Intelligence: explains findings and correlates risk with optional AI. AI never decides a gate result.

In the default install, Preflyt reads and records: It reads repository files and metadata through a read-only GitHub App. It records CI results GitHub reports for exact commits. It does not run your tests or scanners itself. Your own GitHub Actions workflow runs them, and Preflyt verifies the completed run. Native execution inside Preflyt is off until you deploy its separate, reviewed controller. It does not block merges by default. Blocking needs three explicit steps: publish a policy, turn on PR checks, and require the Preflyt / Engineering Readiness check in GitHub. See Pull request checks and Merge Protection. A Related files found result means a supported file or workflow reference exists at that commit. It does not prove the tool ran or passed.

Object Meaning Workspace Your organization's space in Preflyt, linked to a GitHub organization or identity provider. Repository A GitHub repository you have explicitly selected. Profile What Preflyt found in a repository at one commit. Standard A versioned set of engineering checks, such as Application Security. Report (assessment) A saved snapshot of selected standards and evidence at one commit, with a merge review result. CI result A check or workflow outcome GitHub reported for a commit. Finding An issue surfaced from evidence, with its own lifecycle.
Every status in Preflyt has a text label as well as a colour, so meaning never depends on colour alone.

Colour Meaning Green Success, healthy or completed Red Failure or error Amber Needs attention, pending or stale Blue Information or in progress Grey Not run, inactive or not available Green marks a confirmed positive state. Related files found is green because configuration was found; it does not mean a check executed or passed. Unknown is amber and still needs attention.

Shown on the repository Overview. Filter the list with All, Needs review or Files found. Label Meaning Related files found A supported file or workflow reference exists at the inspected commit. Shown in green for configuration found; it is not an execution pass. Not found No supported configuration was found. This is not a policy failure. Unknown Preflyt could not tell, for example because files were unreadable or the check is not implemented.

Shown per check inside a report. Label Meaning Related files found Supporting files were observed at that exact commit. Not found Nothing associated or observed. Source not verified A CI result is associated but its source is not verified. Pending The associated CI result had not finished. Skipped The associated job was not run. Result expired The result was too old at the time of collection. Report date is in the future The result's timestamp is later than expected, so it is not trusted as fresh. Newer result available A later result for the same source replaced it. Multiple matching results Conflicting results with the same or unknown time. Not available The check adapter does not exist yet, so an association cannot enable it. Each check in a report also has a result: Passed, Failed, Incomplete or Not evaluated.

Label Meaning Succeeded GitHub reported success. This does not equal a Preflyt pass. Failed GitHub reported failure. Pending Still running or queued. Not run The job was skipped or did not execute. Unknown GitHub did not report a conclusion.

Label Meaning Recorded The delivery was verified and stored. Waiting to process Stored, and the worker has not processed it yet. Not processed Repository access changed before the worker processed it. Processing failed The worker gave up after repeated attempts. See Troubleshooting.

Every report leads with one merge review result. It comes only from the saved report, so it is repeatable. It is Preflyt's view; whether GitHub allows a merge is decided by GitHub. Result Meaning Required checks passed Every check is met by observed evidence. For configuration checks this confirms configuration only. Optional checks need attention Every required check passes, but an optional check does not. Required checks failed A required check has a failed result from an approved, verified CI source at that commit. Required results incomplete Required evidence is missing, stale or unverified, collection was truncated, or the policy has no required checks. Results that Preflyt cannot verify stay incomplete. They never become a pass.

This section takes you from installation to a first repository report. That first report can reveal configuration and missing evidence; it does not mean your tests have run. To reach a verified PR result, continue through policy and workflow setup below. Quick Start: run a local instance and sign in as Super Admin. Connect GitHub: create the GitHub App, save it in Preflyt and sign in with GitHub. Select repositories: choose what Preflyt may read. Your first report: one click from the Overview, or step by step. Who does what A Super Admin (the recovery account from your .env) configures the deployment: GitHub App credentials, sign-in and notifications. A GitHub organization owner signs in with GitHub and creates the workspace. Workspace Owners and Admins select repositories, adopt standards and create assessments. Other members work within their assigned roles and repository scopes. If you only want to evaluate Preflyt on one machine, follow the pages in order. For a real deployment, do the Self-Hosting setup first.

Create or choose a standard, then create, approve and publish a policy for the branch you target. Repository standards and branch policy versions are separate; saving one does not publish the other. Have the deployment administrator enable event ingestion, PR check publication and automatic checks, and configure a public HTTPS API URL. Enable checks for your repository in Settings → PR feedback. In Policies → CI jobs, copy the workflow snippet or review and create a setup PR. Merge the reviewed workflow change into the target branch through your normal GitHub process. Open a same-repository, non-draft test PR. The workflow runs checks, submits reports and waits in its final gate. Confirm the current head commit has a published Preflyt / Engineering Readiness check and a matching assessment. If wanted, add AI reviews, keeping your chosen provider and explicitly enabling code sharing. Test their publication on a PR. Only after the verified PR path works, optionally activate Merge Protection, or require the check yourself in GitHub. The public Preflyt Action needs no Preflyt API key. One GitHub App is enough. An external report signer, a second governance App and native execution are not prerequisites for this path. Private application images still require registry pull access; the public Action does not grant access to them.

documents.t: Preflyt reads your repositories through a GitHub App that you own. This page connects the App and creates your workspace. Public URL needed for webhooks GitHub cannot call localhost. You can complete every step below locally and use repository profiles and assessments without webhooks. To receive pull request and CI events you need a public HTTPS URL, either a real deployment or a tunnel you control.

Sign in as Super Admin. On Overview choose Configure GitHub, or open Settings → Configuration → GitHub. For a new deployment, choose Create your GitHub App: Enter your GitHub organization and public HTTPS API URL. With the bundled web proxy, use https://preflyt.example.com/api. Enable Create setup PRs if you want Preflyt to propose workflow changes. Enable Manage GitHub rulesets only if you want Preflyt-managed protection. Choose Review App setup, then Confirm in GitHub. GitHub may require a fresh security confirmation (GitHub Mobile, passkey or authenticator). Complete it in the same browser tab, review the App details, and confirm registration. Preflyt supplies the callbacks, permissions and webhook settings. Return to Preflyt. App credentials are stored encrypted automatically, and the API and worker refresh without a restart. Merge protection remains off until explicitly activated. See GitHub App setup for deployment prerequisites and permissions.
documents.s: 1. Create or connect the GitHub App

documents.t: An App already connected to Preflyt does not need to be replaced. Add optional permissions to that same App in GitHub and approve its updated installation. For an App created manually, expand Connect an existing App or edit advanced settings. Save its App ID, client ID, client secret, private key, webhook secret and exact callbacks. Enable GitHub sign-in and event ingestion as needed. Saved GitHub connection changes refresh automatically; no routine restart is needed. The Public Preflyt API URL must be reachable by GitHub Actions and webhooks. Localhost works for a profiles-only trial, but cannot receive GitHub's webhook calls. Use a public HTTPS tunnel for live Action tests. The Quick Start includes distinct CONFIGURATION_ENCRYPTION_KEY and GITHUB_USER_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY values. If an older deployment is missing either key, add it to deployment secrets and run docker compose up -d api worker to recreate the services. A plain restart does not reload .env.

In GitHub, open your App's page and choose Install App, then pick your organization. You can give it all repositories or a chosen set. Preflyt only works with repositories you additionally select inside Preflyt.
documents.s: 3. Install the App on your organization

documents.t: Open Preflyt and sign out of Super Admin. On the sign-in page, choose Continue with GitHub. On Choose your organization, choose Connect organization for your organization. A GitHub organization owner can connect a new workspace. Preflyt verifies that you own the organization. After verification succeeds, Preflyt opens the workspace with your Owner role. Other GitHub organization members can sign in once an Owner grants them a role: Access Control → GitHub members → Assign role. If you use an identity provider instead Organizations that use OIDC single sign-on follow Authentication. The Create legacy workspace action in Access Control exists for existing identity-provider deployments. GitHub workspaces are created through the verified onboarding above.
documents.s: 4. Sign in with GitHub and create the workspace

documents.t: If your workspace already has repositories and policies, its Owner should use Access Control → GitHub members → Link GitHub organization after GitHub sign-in is configured. This preserves the workspace and its history. Do not create a second workspace to migrate an existing one. See Authentication.

Select repositories. For a new self-hosted deployment, the Super Admin can create the App through Settings → Configuration → GitHub using the guided registration flow. See GitHub App setup. Existing Apps use the same connection flow and do not need to be replaced.
A report (an assessment of one commit) shows which checks your repository meets, which fail and which still lack results. You need to be an Owner or Admin and to have selected a repository.

Open Overview. Under Get your first repository report, choose a repository with Select a repository. Choose Create first report. Preflyt then does three things, showing progress as it goes: Inspects the repository if it has not been inspected yet: languages, frameworks and existing CI configuration. Saves the recommended standards for the detected stack, unless you have already chosen your own. Creates the report for the inspected commit. When it finishes you see "Your first report is ready". Missing check results stay visible as missing. Merge blocking and AI source-sharing settings stay as they were.

documents.t: Use this when you want to choose the standards yourself first.

Open Repositories and open a selected repository. Choose Discover profile. Preflyt reads the default branch through the GitHub App and records what it finds at that commit. Nothing is built or run. The Overview tab then shows: a summary of Selected checks, Configuration hints, Recent CI results and Recent assessments, Repository checks, filtered by All, Needs review or Files found, the detected Stack, Tooling and Snapshot (branch, commit and capture time). Related files found means a supported file exists for that check, for example a workflow that mentions a scanner. It is information, not a pass: whether the check actually ran is shown in the report. Open the evidence button on a row to see the files, linked to GitHub at that commit. Partial inspection If Preflyt could not read some files, the header shows Partial inspection. Select it to see why. Checks that depend on unread files show Unknown, not missing. Choose Refresh profile to inspect the latest commit again.

Open the Standards tab and choose Choose standards. Pick a Requirement level: Core (baseline requirements), Recommended (adds broader checks) or Strict (also requires resilience checks). Choose up to five standards. Standards that match the detected stack are marked Recommended. Review the changes Preflyt shows, then choose Save standards. Saving standards does not turn on GitHub merge protection, and existing branch policies keep their approved version until you publish a new revision.

Open the Assessments tab and choose New assessment. The commit is filled with the inspected commit. You can enter another full 40-character SHA that Preflyt has a profile or CI result for. Under CI result per control, leave Use the approved CI source if available unless you need to link a specific result by hand. Choose Create assessment. Manual links are your claim A CI result you link by hand is recorded as unverified. It never turns into a pass on its own. See Evidence and trust.

Open a row in Saved assessments to see the report: The Merge review result at the top: Required checks passed, Required checks failed, Required results incomplete or Optional checks need attention. A Next step telling you what to do. Failed and incomplete required checks first. Passing and optional checks are available through the filter. Source and verification details for the digests of everything the report saved. Reports are historical: each one describes a single commit. If your GitHub App receives pull request events, Preflyt also creates reports automatically for pull request commits in repositories with saved standards.
Make this run on every pull request: Pull request checks. Read How Preflyt works and Status labels. Set up webhooks to collect CI results automatically. Invite your team from Access Control.

Run Preflyt on your own machine with Docker Compose. You download one file, create one settings file and start it. You do not need the Preflyt source code. This is a local trial on http://localhost:8080. For a deployment other people use, follow Docker Compose.

You need: Docker with Compose 2.23.1 or later. Check with docker compose version. curl and openssl, which macOS and Linux include. Access to the Preflyt images. They are stored privately at ghcr.io/lyrisoft. You need a GitHub account that has been given read access to those packages, and a personal access token (classic) with the read:packages permission. If you do not have access, ask Lyrisoft. The release to run. Use a published stable version such as vX.Y.Z, or a development build identified by sha- followed by the 40-character commit ID. Choose an existing tag from the release you were given.
docker login ghcr.io -u YOUR_GITHUB_USERNAME # Paste your read:packages token at the Password prompt. You should see Login Succeeded.

Create each with: openssl rand -hex 24 POSTGRES_PASSWORD=REPLACE_WITH_RANDOM_HEX DATABASE_APP_PASSWORD=REPLACE_WITH_A_DIFFERENT_RANDOM_HEX # REQUIRED. Keep copies outside the server. Lets Preflyt run over plain http://localhost. # Never set these on a deployment other people can reach. PREFLYT_NODE_ENV=development PREFLYT_COOKIE_SECURE=false Create the random values with these commands and paste each result in: openssl rand -hex 24 # POSTGRES_PASSWORD, then again for DATABASE_APP_PASSWORD openssl rand -hex 20 # a strong SUPER_ADMIN_PASSWORD openssl rand -base64 32 # CONFIGURATION_ENCRYPTION_KEY, then again for GITHUB_USER_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY Finally make the file private: chmod 600 .env This command writes .env for you with freshly generated passwords and keys. Set PREFLYT_VERSION to the release you were given. Keep this file safe CONFIGURATION_ENCRYPTION_KEY protects the credentials you save in Settings later. If you lose it, those credentials cannot be recovered. Keep a copy somewhere safe, apart from the database. Local trial only PREFLYT_NODE_ENV=development and PREFLYT_COOKIE_SECURE=false let Preflyt run over plain http://localhost. Never use them on a deployment other people can reach.

docker compose up -d --wait The first start pulls the images, which can take a few minutes. When it finishes, check that every service is healthy: docker compose ps api, worker, web, db, cache and queue should all show healthy.

Open http://localhost:8080. On a fresh install the page says Set up Preflyt. Choose Start setup and sign in with admin and the password from your .env. You land on the Engineering Overview, which shows Connect your organization. Choose Configure GitHub to continue with Connect GitHub.

The Super Admin configures the deployment: GitHub App credentials, single sign-on, email and feature switches in Settings → Configuration. It is not a member of any workspace. Until a GitHub organization owner creates the workspace, the sidebar shows Select organization / Organization setup, and workspace pages such as Standards show that you do not have access. That is expected.

documents.t: docker compose stop # stop, keeping your data docker compose up -d # start again docker compose down # remove containers, keeping your data Your data lives in Docker volumes and survives all of the above. Do not run docker compose down --volumes unless you want to delete everything.

What you see What to do required variable PREFLYT_VERSION is missing a value Set PREFLYT_VERSION in .env to an existing stable version (vX.Y.Z) or development SHA tag. error from registry: unauthorized while pulling You are not signed in, or the account cannot read the Preflyt packages. Repeat step 1 with a token that has read:packages. Docker shows this message for a wrong release ID too, so check both. An error that mentions configs or content Your Docker Compose is older than 2.23.1. Update Docker. A service is unhealthy Run docker compose logs api worker and see Troubleshooting.
Connect GitHub.
Installing the GitHub App makes repositories available. Preflyt only works with the ones you select. This keeps the scope explicit and auditable.

Open Repositories in the sidebar. The summary tiles show Available repositories, Selected for Preflyt, Active installations and Private repositories. Below, each repository is a card. Tick the checkbox in the corner of a card to select it. Use Search repositories and the selection and visibility filters to narrow a long list. Selected repositories link to their own page. Select one to open it. Only a Preflyt Owner or Admin can change selection. Other roles see the inventory without the checkboxes, and attempting the change returns "Only a Preflyt Owner or Admin can change repository selection." If the list is empty, check that: the GitHub App is installed on the organization and has access to those repositories, the Super Admin saved the App credentials and restarted the API and worker, you are signed in with a role that can connect repositories. Use Refresh repositories to re-read the list from GitHub. The page otherwise shows the last successful sync. If GitHub reports that the App lost access to repositories, the page tells you to reconnect the App to restore it.

Selecting lets Preflyt read the repository's metadata and file contents to build a profile, and lets webhook events for it be recorded. Events for repositories that are not selected are acknowledged and discarded. Selecting does not run any repository code, build or test. Selecting does not give other people access. Access comes from roles and repository assignment in Access Control.
documents.s: What selecting does and does not do

documents.t: Your first report. Selecting a repository automatically inspects its files to detect the stack. It does not execute code. Recommended checks are preselected when you open Choose standards for a repository without a saved selection; existing standards, published policies and model routing are preserved. If inspection fails, the repository stays selected and Refresh profile lets you retry.
Preflyt runs entirely as containers. The same application images run under Docker Compose or Kubernetes; only the manifests differ.

Service Purpose web nginx serving the web app. It forwards /api/ to the API on the same origin. This is the only service that publishes a host port. api The application API: sign-in, repositories, standards, assessments, webhooks. worker Background processing: webhook events, CI evidence, reconciliation and notifications. migrate A one-shot job that applies database migrations before the API starts. db PostgreSQL 16. The source of truth for all Preflyt data. cache Valkey (Redis-compatible), 128 MB, evicting, no persistence. Metadata cache only. queue A separate Valkey with noeviction and AOF persistence for the job queue. otel-collector Optional OpenTelemetry collector, started with the observability profile. Only web is reachable from the host, and only on loopback (127.0.0.1:8080 by default). The API, database, cache and queue have no host ports.

Docker Engine or Docker Desktop with Compose 2.23.1 or later. A GitHub organization where you can create a GitHub App. Preflyt connects to GitHub only through this App. For production: a host HTTPS reverse proxy and a public origin such as https://preflyt.example.com. See Reverse proxy and TLS. Preflyt does not install certificates for you. Optionally, an OpenID Connect provider if you want single sign-on. Node.js, pnpm, PostgreSQL and Redis do not need to be installed on the host.

Option Use it for Docker Compose A single host. The recommended starting point for evaluation and small teams. Kubernetes A single-instance bundle for clusters. Ingress, TLS, storage backups and capacity are your responsibility. Images Preflyt runs from container images stored privately at ghcr.io/lyrisoft. You need an account with read access to those packages, and you sign in with docker login ghcr.io. You do not need the source code. Stable releases use vX.Y.Z image tags; development builds use sha- plus the 40-character commit ID. Choose an existing published tag.

Preflyt does not provide your TLS certificate, DNS, off-host backups or monitoring backend. It also does not run repository code or scanners in the default stack: native execution stays disabled until you deploy its separate, reviewed controller. See Evidence and trust.

Preflyt supports three ways to sign in. You can use any combination. Method Best for Configured in Super Admin recovery login First setup, and recovery if other sign-in breaks Environment variables GitHub sign-in Teams that already manage access through a GitHub organization GitHub App plus Settings → Configuration Single sign-on (OIDC) Organizations with an identity provider Settings → Configuration

Set both values in .env before the first start: SUPER_ADMIN_USERNAME=admin SUPER_ADMIN_PASSWORD=<24 to 128 characters> On startup Preflyt seeds one Super Admin account and stores only a salted scrypt hash of the password. Sign in at: <WEB_ORIGIN>/super-admin/login Properties of this login: It is rate-limited and audited. A session lasts 24 hours from sign-in. Activity does not extend it. Restarting the API with the same database and credentials keeps existing sessions. Changing or removing the configured credentials revokes local sessions. Super Admin is the only role that can open Settings → Configuration. Keep it available If other sign-in methods are misconfigured, the Super Admin login is how you get back in. Keep the credentials in your secret manager even after you set up GitHub or SSO. If you configure no OIDC and GitHub sign-in is off, Preflyt runs in recovery-only mode. A fresh install needs this login first, because the settings for the other methods live behind it.

GitHub sign-in lets verified members of your GitHub organization sign in, and lets an Owner grant roles by GitHub username. Accounts are never matched by email or username, and existing identities are never merged automatically. Before enabling it: Install the GitHub App in your organization with Organization members: Read-only. In the App, enable Expire user authorization tokens and register the login callback: <WEB_ORIGIN>/api/auth/github/callback Generate a separate token key and add it to .env: openssl rand -base64 32 # set as GITHUB_USER_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY Recreate the API and worker after adding the environment key: docker compose up -d api worker. A plain restart does not load changed .env values. In Settings → Configuration → GitHub, save the App ID, client ID and secret, private key and the exact login callback. Turn on GitHub sign-in. Restart the API and the worker. Then a verified GitHub organization owner can sign in and create the matching workspace, and grant members access from Access Control → GitHub members. How GitHub sessions behave: A GitHub session has an absolute eight-hour maximum. Refreshing GitHub tokens never extends a Preflyt session. Access evidence expires after five minutes, and privileged changes need fresh verification. If GitHub is briefly unavailable, existing credentials and your session are kept. A revoked authorization or an expired refresh token means you must sign in again. Turning sign-in off hides it from new users. It does not delete links, grants or audit records. To link an existing workspace to a GitHub organization, use Access Control → GitHub members → Link GitHub organization. It checks the current workspace Owner and a GitHub organization owner before confirming, keeps your repositories, policies and history, and records the grant in the audit log.

In your identity provider, register the callback: <WEB_ORIGIN>/api/auth/callback In Settings → Configuration → Single sign-on, enter the issuer, client ID and client secret, and the callback. All four fields are required together. Restart the API and the worker. Create the first Owner with an out-of-band token. Generate a high-entropy secret, publish its SHA-256 as BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN_SHA256 in .env, and enter the original token on the setup screen at <WEB_ORIGIN>/setup. Partial configuration blocks startup If only some OIDC fields are set, or discovery against the issuer fails, startup is blocked. Provide all fields or none. Production requires HTTPS issuer and callback URLs. An enabled provider is validated at startup, so a wrong value shows up as a failed API start, not as a broken sign-in page later.

Production forces secure cookies. Use the same browser hostname throughout: localhost and 127.0.0.1 keep separate cookies. If the page cannot confirm your session (for example during an API restart), you see Reconnect to Preflyt and a Retry connection button. Preflyt sends you to sign-in only after a confirmed sign-out or a 401. Session validity and revocation come from PostgreSQL, not Redis.

documents.t: Preflyt splits configuration in two: Settings → Configuration in the web app holds application connections and feature switches. Only a Super Admin can change them. They apply to every workspace. Environment variables hold everything that must exist before the database can be read: infrastructure, encryption keys and trust controls.

Open Settings → Configuration as Super Admin. Section What you configure GitHub Public Preflyt API URL, App ID, client ID and secret, private key, webhook secret, installation and login callbacks, the sign-in switch and the event-ingestion switch Governance An optional separate governance App and installation ID, automatic PR check publication, ruleset activation, history import and retention Single sign-on OIDC issuer, client ID and secret, callback Notifications In-app and email switches, SMTP host, port, sender, username and password Intelligence Model configuration and advisory review switches Native execution Preflight and execution switches Organization-level settings stay on their own pages: AI models and provider keys, review skills, CI jobs and policies, notification channels, and Settings → PR feedback (PR check publication, policy summary comments and optional AI feedback). Organization Owners and Admins cannot change deployment credentials.

Secrets stay hidden. The browser never receives a saved secret, only whether one is set. Leave a secret field empty to keep the saved value. Use Clear saved and then Save changes to remove it. GitHub connections refresh safely. GitHub and optional governance credentials apply immediately in the API and within five seconds in the worker. Cached App clients and installation tokens refresh when the App key changes. OIDC and SMTP connections still require an API and worker restart; the page shows a restart notice for those changes. Feature switches apply on their own. Switches and history retention refresh every five seconds, with no restart. Concurrent edits are detected. If someone else saved first, refresh and re-apply your change. Changes are audited. The audit record stores who changed which fields and the revision, never secret values. Failures fail closed. If a read or decryption fails, live switches turn off until a read succeeds. Preflyt does not fall back to old environment values. Environment-file edits are different: use docker compose up -d to recreate affected services. docker compose restart does not reload .env.

On first start the API imports any application values it finds in the environment once, encrypts the secrets and stores them. After that, database values always win, including empty ones. On a fresh install you can leave the application values out and fill them in under Settings. You will first need the Super Admin recovery login to open the page. See Authentication.

Keep these in your .env or secret manager: database and migration passwords, cache and queue URLs and prefixes, the public origin and HTTP port, the Super Admin recovery credentials and bootstrap token, telemetry, the three encryption keys, native execution, CI proof and attestation trust settings.

Generate three separate 32-byte base64 keys with openssl rand -base64 32: Key Protects CONFIGURATION_ENCRYPTION_KEY Credentials saved in Settings → Configuration GITHUB_USER_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY GitHub user tokens used for GitHub sign-in AI_PROVIDER_ENCRYPTION_KEY AI provider credentials Never reuse one key for another purpose, commit a value, or paste a key into Settings. Back up each key in your secret manager, independently of the database. There is no key rotation: if you replace a key, restore the original to decrypt what it protected.
Defaults are what Preflyt uses when you do not set a value. A blank default means the value is unset. You only need to set the variables in the Docker Compose guide to get started.

Variable Default Description WEB_ORIGIN https://preflyt.example.com Public origin, no trailing slash or path. Production requires HTTPS. PREFLYT_HTTP_PORT 8080 Loopback port the web service publishes. PREFLYT_IMAGE_REGISTRY ghcr.io/lyrisoft Where the images are pulled from. PREFLYT_VERSION Required. An existing stable version (vX.Y.Z) or development tag (sha- plus the 40-character commit ID). POSTGRES_PASSWORD Database owner password, used by migrations. Hexadecimal. DATABASE_APP_PASSWORD Runtime database role password. Hexadecimal and different from the owner password. CONFIGURATION_ENCRYPTION_KEY Encrypts credentials saved in Settings. Required.

Variable Default Description SUPER_ADMIN_USERNAME Recovery username. Set together with the password to seed the account. SUPER_ADMIN_PASSWORD Recovery password, 24 to 128 characters. Stored only as a salted scrypt hash. BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN_SHA256 SHA-256 hex of your out-of-band first-Owner token, for the OIDC first-Owner flow. GITHUB_USER_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY Base64 of 32 random bytes. Required to enable GitHub sign-in.

Variable Default Description REDIS_URL redis://cache:6379/0 Metadata cache. Override only for a separately managed service. REDIS_CACHE_PREFIX preflyt:production:cache Key prefix for the cache. QUEUE_REDIS_URL redis://queue:6379/0 Job queue. It must not evict keys. QUEUE_PREFIX preflyt:production:queue Key prefix for the queue. Keep the queue separate The cache evicts under memory pressure. The queue must use noeviction with persistence. Do not point both at the same evicting instance. Different Redis database numbers do not isolate memory.

Telemetry is off until you provide an endpoint. See Observability. Variable Default Description OTEL_SDK_DISABLED true Set to false to enable OpenTelemetry. OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT OTLP base endpoint. OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL http/protobuf http/protobuf or grpc. OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS Encoded exporter headers. OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT Full traces URL (HTTP includes /v1/traces). OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_METRICS_ENDPOINT Full metrics URL. OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_LOGS_ENDPOINT Full logs URL. OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TIMEOUT 3000 Export timeout in milliseconds. OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER otlp Traces exporter. OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER otlp Metrics exporter. OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER otlp Logs exporter. OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES service.namespace=preflyt,deployment.environment.name=production Resource attributes. OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER parentbased_traceidratio Sampler. OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER_ARG 0.1 Sampling ratio. OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_INTERVAL 60000 Metric export interval in milliseconds. OTEL_PROPAGATORS tracecontext,baggage Context propagators. COLLECTOR_UPSTREAM_ENDPOINT OTLP HTTP base URL the optional collector forwards to. COLLECTOR_UPSTREAM_HEADERS {} JSON object of upstream headers, for example {"Authorization":"Bearer <token>"}.
Variable Default Description SMTP_ALLOW_INSECURE_LOCAL false Development only. Allows a loopback SMTP server without TLS. Ignored in production.

Normal Action onboarding verifies the GitHub run, attempt, commit and completed jobs directly through the GitHub App. Report signatures are optional, including for private repositories; no GPG key or external signer is required. The variables below configure additional signed-report verification for deployments that explicitly use it. See the advanced trust runbook; it is not the basic onboarding path. Variable Default Description CI_REPORT_PROOF_MODE github-native Verification of optional report signatures: GitHub attestations (github-native) or a configured organization signer (organization-key). Neither is required for the normal GitHub job-verification path. CI_ORGANIZATION_SIGNER_KEYS Public-key allowlist JSON. Never include private keys. CI_ATTESTATION_GH_PATH Absolute container path of the reviewed GitHub CLI executable used to verify attestations. CI_ATTESTATION_GH_SHA256 SHA-256 of that exact binary, lowercase hexadecimal. CI_ATTESTATION_ROOT_PATH Absolute container path of the reviewed Sigstore trusted-root file. CI_ATTESTATION_ROOT_SHA256 SHA-256 of that exact file, lowercase hexadecimal. CI_ATTESTATION_WORKFLOWS JSON array of exact signer workflow paths, owner/repo/.github/workflows/file.yml. CI_EXECUTION_CONTRACTS Reviewed JSON array of contracts. Each pins a rule ID, signer workflow, reviewed commit, report format and tool version. Set by the deployer, never by users. PREFLYT_ATTESTATION_DIR Host directory mounted by the reviewed evidence Compose override. GITHUB_GOVERNANCE_LOCAL_ACCEPTANCE false Must stay false in production. For disposable local acceptance only.

Native execution is disabled by default and needs its own reviewed controller. See Native execution for prerequisites, supported adapters and remaining acceptance limits. Variable Default Description NATIVE_RUNTIME_BACKEND kubernetes Explicit runtime backend: kubernetes or docker. No fallback after failed review. NATIVE_DOCKER_APPROVAL Signed independent approval for the Docker backend; use instead of a Kubernetes runtime approval. NATIVE_RUNTIME_APPROVAL A signed independent review of the execution runtime (an Ed25519 signed token). It expires within 30 days. NATIVE_RUNTIME_REVIEW_KEYS [] JSON array of trusted Ed25519 public keys (kid and PEM) that verify that review. NATIVE_CONTROLLER_API_KEY Random key of 32 to 256 characters shared by the API, worker and execution controller. NATIVE_TOOL_REVIEWS [] JSON array of reviewed tools: rule, image pinned by @sha256: digest, version, licence, configuration hash and expiry (at most 30 days). Repository-supplied commands are never accepted.

Variable Default Description AI_PROVIDER_ENCRYPTION_KEY Base64 of 32 random bytes. Separate from every other key. Models and endpoints are created by organization admins under AI Intelligence, not in the environment.

This page installs Preflyt on one server for a team to use. You download one compose file, create one settings file and start it. You do not need the Preflyt source code. For a quick look on your own machine first, use the Quick Start.

A Linux server (or any host) with Docker and Compose 2.23.1 or later. Check with docker compose version. Access to the Preflyt images at ghcr.io/lyrisoft. They are private. You need a GitHub account that has been given read access to those packages and a personal access token (classic) with read:packages. Ask Lyrisoft if you do not have access. A release to run. Use a published stable version (vX.Y.Z) or a development build (sha- plus the 40-character commit ID). A public HTTPS address for Preflyt, such as https://preflyt.example.com, and a reverse proxy that serves it. See Reverse proxy and TLS.
docker login ghcr.io -u YOUR_GITHUB_USERNAME # Paste your read:packages token at the Password prompt.
