Your public HTTPS address: no trailing slash, no path. WEB_ORIGIN=https://preflyt.example.com # Super Admin sign-in. The password must be 24 to 128 characters. SUPER_ADMIN_USERNAME=admin SUPER_ADMIN_PASSWORD=REPLACE_WITH_24_TO_128_CHARACTERS # REQUIRED. Two different random values. Create each with: openssl rand -hex 24 POSTGRES_PASSWORD=REPLACE_WITH_RANDOM_HEX DATABASE_APP_PASSWORD=REPLACE_WITH_A_DIFFERENT_RANDOM_HEX # REQUIRED. Keep copies outside the server. Generate a separate value for each key. # Create each with: openssl rand -base64 32 CONFIGURATION_ENCRYPTION_KEY=REPLACE_WITH_RANDOM_BASE64 GITHUB_USER_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY=REPLACE_WITH_A_DIFFERENT_RANDOM_BASE64 # Optional AI reviews: add AI_PROVIDER_ENCRYPTION_KEY with a third separate key. Create the random values with these commands and paste each result in: openssl rand -hex 24 # POSTGRES_PASSWORD, then again for DATABASE_APP_PASSWORD openssl rand -hex 20 # a strong SUPER_ADMIN_PASSWORD openssl rand -base64 32 # CONFIGURATION_ENCRYPTION_KEY, then again for GITHUB_USER_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY Finally make the file private: chmod 600 .env This command writes .env for you with freshly generated passwords and keys. Replace REPLACE_WITH_PUBLISHED_VERSION with your release first. cat > .env <<EOF PREFLYT_VERSION=REPLACE_WITH_PUBLISHED_VERSION WEB_ORIGIN=https://preflyt.example.com SUPER_ADMIN_USERNAME=admin SUPER_ADMIN_PASSWORD=$(openssl rand -hex 20) POSTGRES_PASSWORD=$(openssl rand -hex 24) DATABASE_APP_PASSWORD=$(openssl rand -hex 24) CONFIGURATION_ENCRYPTION_KEY=$(openssl rand -base64 32) GITHUB_USER_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY=$(openssl rand -base64 32) EOF chmod 600 .env Read your sign-in password with grep SUPER_ADMIN_PASSWORD .env. Set PREFLYT_VERSION to the release you were given, and WEB_ORIGIN to your public HTTPS address with no trailing slash and no path. Back up your keys now CONFIGURATION_ENCRYPTION_KEY decrypts the credentials you save in Settings → Configuration. If you lose or replace it, those credentials cannot be recovered. Preflyt has no key rotation. Copy .env to your secret manager before you continue. Passwords are set once POSTGRES_PASSWORD and DATABASE_APP_PASSWORD only take effect when the database is first created. Changing them later does not change the existing database's passwords.

docker compose up -d --wait docker compose ps Startup follows health checks: PostgreSQL becomes healthy. The migrate job applies the database migrations and exits. The API starts and becomes ready. The worker starts and waits for the API's configuration. The web service starts. A migration failure stops the API and web from starting. Read docker compose logs migrate.
Preflyt listens only on 127.0.0.1:8080 of the server. Set up your reverse proxy so your public address forwards to it. See Reverse proxy and TLS.
documents.s: 5. Put HTTPS in front of it

documents.t: Open your WEB_ORIGIN in a browser. You should see Set up Preflyt. Choose Start setup and sign in with admin and your SUPER_ADMIN_PASSWORD. Check the health endpoint: curl -fsS https://preflyt.example.com/healthz should print ok. This does not test your GitHub setup. Continue with Connect GitHub.

Data Where Database The postgres_data volume Job queue The queue_data volume Cache Memory only. Safe to lose. docker compose stop and docker compose down keep your data. Do not delete the volumes Never run docker compose down --volumes on an installation whose data you need. Containers run as non-root with read-only filesystems, dropped capabilities and no-new-privileges. The runtime database role can read and write data only: it has no superuser, role-creation or database-creation rights.
Connect GitHub Authentication Upgrades and backups Observability

Preflyt connects to GitHub through a GitHub App that you create and own. The App decides what Preflyt can see. Preflyt never asks for a personal access token. One App is enough Preflyt uses the same App for reading repositories, publishing pull request checks and managing member access. The same App can also manage rulesets when you grant Organization administration: Read and write and enable ruleset activation. A second, separately credentialed governance App is optional for deployments that want separate credentials and permissions. Normal onboarding does not require it.

Sign in as Super Admin and open Settings → Configuration → GitHub → Create your GitHub App. Enter your GitHub organization and the public HTTPS API URL. With the bundled web proxy, use <WEB_ORIGIN>/api. Leave optional capabilities off unless you want Preflyt to Create setup PRs or Manage GitHub rulesets. The default App can read repositories and workflow results, verify organization membership, and publish checks and advisory PR reviews. Choose Review App setup, then Confirm in GitHub. GitHub registers the App with Preflyt's permissions, callbacks and webhook settings. GitHub returns you to Preflyt. Credentials are saved encrypted, without copying keys or restarting the API and worker. Install the App, then open Integrations to connect it and explicitly select repositories. The deployment needs distinct CONFIGURATION_ENCRYPTION_KEY and GITHUB_USER_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY values and a configured QUEUE_REDIS_URL before registration. Generate them during deployment setup; credentials are not returned to the browser. GitHub confirmation is bound to the original administrator session and expires after 30 minutes. If confirmation cannot be saved, check for the registered App in GitHub before retrying. An existing App is never replaced by this wizard. Use Connect an existing App or edit advanced settings for manual configuration. Add optional permissions to the same App in GitHub and approve its updated installation. Merge protection remains off until explicitly activated, and model routing is preserved. GitHub sign-in requires expiring user authorization tokens; verify that the newly registered App keeps this GitHub setting enabled.
documents.s: Recommended: create the App from Preflyt

documents.t: In GitHub, open your organization's Settings → Developer settings → GitHub Apps → New GitHub App, then set: Field Value GitHub App name A name you choose, for example Preflyt (Acme) Homepage URL Your WEB_ORIGIN Callback URL <WEB_ORIGIN>/api/github/oauth/callback and, to allow GitHub sign-in, <WEB_ORIGIN>/api/auth/github/callback Expire user authorization tokens Enabled (needed for GitHub sign-in) Request user authorization (OAuth) during installation Disabled Setup URL <WEB_ORIGIN>/api/github/setup/callback Webhook: Active Enabled Webhook URL <WEB_ORIGIN>/api/github/webhooks Webhook secret A random string of at least 32 characters: openssl rand -hex 32 Leave "Request user authorization during installation" off Preflyt runs its own state- and PKCE-bound authorization step after installation and checks that the installing GitHub user can access the installation. Enabling GitHub's option interferes with that flow. GitHub cannot deliver webhooks to localhost. For local trials, expose your instance through an HTTPS tunnel you control, or leave event ingestion off and inspect repository profiles and create assessments. Without reachable webhooks and a public API, this does not exercise automatic PR checks. There is no manual report-import step in onboarding.

Repository permissions Permission Access Used for Metadata Read-only Required by GitHub. Repository discovery. Contents Read-only Repository profiles and file evidence. Pull requests Read and write Reading pull requests, and posting the optional policy summary and AI review comments. Read-only is enough if you turn those off. Actions Read-only Verifying completed GitHub Actions runs. Checks Read and write Publishing the Preflyt / Engineering Readiness check on pull requests, and reading check results. Organization permissions Permission Access Used for Members Read-only The member directory, GitHub sign-in, role grants and team import. Only if you use the guided setup pull request: Preflyt can open a pull request that adds the Preflyt workflow to a repository. That needs Contents, Workflows and Pull requests set to Read and write. Preflyt never edits your default branch directly. If you prefer, copy the workflow yourself and keep Contents read-only. Only if Preflyt manages GitHub organization rulesets: Organization administration: Read and write. Leave it off otherwise. See Merge Protection. Preflyt uses short-lived installation tokens limited to what each action needs. Installation tokens are never stored in the database or sent to the browser.

Under Subscribe to events, select: Event Used for Pull request Pull requests and their automatic reports Check run CI check results Workflow run GitHub Actions results Pull request review Contributor activity Push Contributor activity Organization, Team and Membership Keeping imported GitHub teams and access current. Needs Members read access. GitHub also sends authorization-revocation events to every App automatically. Preflyt accepts pull request, check run and workflow run actions it supports and acknowledges the rest without keeping them.
On the App page, note the App ID and Client ID, create a client secret, and generate a private key (a PEM file). You will paste these into Preflyt.

Sign in as Super Admin and open Settings → Configuration → GitHub: Enter the App ID, client ID, client secret and the private key. A multi-line PEM can be pasted directly into the secret field. Enter the webhook secret you chose above. Confirm the installation and login callbacks match what you registered in GitHub exactly. Turn on GitHub event ingestion to start recording webhooks. Optionally set Public Preflyt API URL: the public HTTPS address of your API that GitHub Actions runners use for Preflyt workflow snippets. With the bundled web proxy, use <WEB_ORIGIN>/api, for example https://preflyt.example.com/api. Localhost is rejected. This field applies without a restart. Save. GitHub connection changes apply immediately in the API and within five seconds in the worker; no routine restart is needed. Callback defaults are derived from WEB_ORIGIN only for the one-time import of legacy values. Saved callbacks must match the deployed origin and the App registration.
Install the App on your organization, then continue with Connect GitHub and Select repositories.

Every delivery is verified with HMAC-SHA256 over the original bytes before anything else happens, and stored before Preflyt answers. Response Meaning 202 accepted Verified and recorded. 202 with accepted:false Unsupported event or action, or a repository that is not selected. Not retained. 401 Invalid signature. Check that the webhook secret matches on both sides. 409 A delivery ID was reused with different bytes. 413 Body over 1 MiB. 503 Event ingestion is off or not configured. Preflyt keeps identifiers, the exact head commit, status, timestamps, the delivery ID and payload digest. It discards raw bodies, pull request text, CI logs, sender details, tokens and arbitrary URLs.

Use a fresh deployment or an isolated test instance with its own database, queue and encryption keys. Do not clear an existing App connection to test onboarding. Sign in as Super Admin and open Settings → Configuration → GitHub. The page must show Create your GitHub App. Enter an organization you own, a unique App name and a reachable public HTTPS API URL. Review the optional setup-PR and ruleset permissions before continuing. Choose Review App setup → Confirm in GitHub. If GitHub asks to confirm access, complete the Mobile, passkey or authenticator challenge in the same browser session. This is GitHub's security confirmation, not a Preflyt credential-copying step. Confirm App registration in GitHub. The browser must return to Preflyt and show Connected. No App private key, client secret or webhook secret should need manual copying. Install the new App on only the test repository. Sign in through GitHub, confirm your organization and select that repository in Preflyt. Its file inspection should complete without running repository code. Check a genuine GitHub webhook delivery and a test PR using the generated workflow. Confirm the delivery is accepted, the PR results use its current commit, and any configured AI review uses the existing model route. Protection must remain off unless separately activated. Record the App name, test repository, date, successful stages and any incomplete stages. Keep secrets, authorization codes and session cookies out of screenshots and reports. Registration alone does not prove repository access, webhook processing or PR publication. Treat those as separate acceptance steps. The manifest confirmation expires after 30 minutes and is bound to the original Super Admin browser session. If it expires, start again from Preflyt. If GitHub already created the App but Preflyt could not save it, inspect that App before retrying; do not create repeated registrations blindly.

Fresh registration was tested on 2026-10-11 with a private test App installed only on the acceptance repository. GitHub confirmation returned to Preflyt; credentials were saved encrypted automatically. The API used the new connection without restarting. GitHub owner sign-in, workspace creation, explicit repository selection, automatic file inspection and processing of two genuine GitHub check events passed. This result covers registration and onboarding. It does not establish a new AI review or policy-gated PR publication result. The test used a temporary webhook tunnel; production needs a stable public HTTPS API URL. GitHub required Mobile re-authentication before App creation, and separate approval before installing the App on the selected repository.

Available as a single-instance manifest bundle. It is rendered and fixture-tested, but not accepted on a live production cluster. Helm and Operator packaging are planned and not implemented. The bundle (the kubernetes folder) uses the same web, API, worker and migration images as Docker Compose. It includes PostgreSQL, a disposable cache and a persistent queue, so a managed database is optional.

A cluster and an explicitly selected kubectl context. Never rely on your current context. An Ingress and TLS controller for the web Service on port 8080. The API and databases stay internal. Registry access to the private images, and a release to run. Storage with backups, and capacity planning. Database and queue storage use retained PVCs on the default storage class. The namespace enforces restricted Pod Security. No host ports, host paths, cluster roles or application service-account tokens are installed.

mkdir preflyt-k8s && cd preflyt-k8s curl -fsSLO https://lyrisoft.github.io/preflyt/downloads/kubernetes.tgz tar -xzf kubernetes.tgz && cd kubernetes The folder contains kustomization.yaml, resources.yaml and migration.yaml.

Create the namespace preflyt, and a pull secret so the cluster can read the private images. Use a token with read:packages from an account that can read the Preflyt packages: kubectl --context YOUR_CONTEXT create namespace preflyt kubectl --context YOUR_CONTEXT -n preflyt create secret docker-registry ghcr-pull \ --docker-server=ghcr.io --docker-username=YOUR_GITHUB_USERNAME --docker-password=YOUR_TOKEN kubectl --context YOUR_CONTEXT -n preflyt patch serviceaccount default \ -p '{"imagePullSecrets":[{"name":"ghcr-pull"}]}' Set the release. The images are tagged :development as a placeholder. Replace the tag with an existing stable version (vX.Y.Z) or development SHA tag: sed -i.bak -E 's#(ghcr\.io/lyrisoft/preflyt-[a-z-]+):development#\1:YOUR_PUBLISHED_VERSION#' resources.yaml migration.yaml For stronger guarantees, use the image digest instead of the tag. The API and worker must use the same API image. Set WEB_ORIGIN in the preflyt-config ConfigMap to your public HTTPS origin. Create the Secrets in the next table from protected files or your secret manager, not shell arguments. Secret Required values preflyt-db-secrets POSTGRES_PASSWORD, DATABASE_APP_PASSWORD preflyt-migration-secrets DATABASE_URL for the preflyt_owner role at db:5432/preflyt preflyt-api-secrets DATABASE_URL for preflyt_app; CONFIGURATION_ENCRYPTION_KEY; the identity and provider encryption keys; deployment trust settings preflyt-worker-secrets DATABASE_URL for preflyt_app; the same CONFIGURATION_ENCRYPTION_KEY; provider keys; CI proof and telemetry settings Use fresh URL-safe passwords. The URLs and password Secrets must agree. Editing a Secret does not rotate a password in an existing database. Application pods never receive the migration owner credentials, and the web pod receives no application Secrets. Provision GitHub, sign-in and notification settings in Settings → Configuration, as for Compose. See Configuration.

All application Deployments start at zero replicas on purpose, so nothing starts before a successful migration. Preview the rendered manifests without cluster access: kubectl kustomize . > rendered.yaml Then, replacing YOUR_CONTEXT: kubectl --context YOUR_CONTEXT apply -k . kubectl --context YOUR_CONTEXT -n preflyt rollout status statefulset/db --timeout=180s kubectl --context YOUR_CONTEXT -n preflyt rollout status statefulset/queue --timeout=180s kubectl --context YOUR_CONTEXT -n preflyt rollout status deployment/cache --timeout=180s kubectl --context YOUR_CONTEXT apply -f migration.yaml kubectl --context YOUR_CONTEXT -n preflyt wait --for=condition=complete job/preflyt-migrate --timeout=600s # Continue only if the migration completed successfully. kubectl --context YOUR_CONTEXT -n preflyt scale deployment/api deployment/worker deployment/web --replicas=1 kubectl --context YOUR_CONTEXT -n preflyt rollout status deployment/api --timeout=180s kubectl --context YOUR_CONTEXT -n preflyt rollout status deployment/worker --timeout=180s kubectl --context YOUR_CONTEXT -n preflyt rollout status deployment/web --timeout=180s The migration Job has no retry and a ten-minute deadline. A failed Job does not authorize scaling up. Keep its logs, and never reset the database or mark a migration applied without repair.

Use a maintenance rollout: Preserve the old image digests, and take and rehearse a protected database backup. Review schema compatibility, then scale API, worker and web to zero. Update images and configuration, apply the bundle, remove only the previous completed migration Job (after saving its diagnostics), and run the new migration Job. Scale up only after the migration succeeds. Do not delete PVCs or queue or database data during an upgrade. Applying the base bundle resets replicas to zero by design, so follow the sequence above rather than applying it casually to a running installation. Restore into a new database before a recovery cutover. Saved GitHub and governance connections refresh immediately in the API and within five seconds in workers. OIDC and SMTP edits still require restarting all API and worker replicas. Coordinate authentication restarts to avoid mixed snapshots. For environment changes, update the deployment configuration and roll out new pods; restarting a pod alone does not change its configuration.

Native execution stays disabled by default. Scanner jobs belong in a dedicated, reviewed execution environment, not the application namespace. Do not give the API or worker Kubernetes Job or Docker control as a shortcut.

Preflyt emits traces, metrics and structured logs using OpenTelemetry. Telemetry is off by default until you supply an endpoint. No particular backend is bundled or required. The API and the worker report under different service names, so you can tell them apart.

In .env: OTEL_SDK_DISABLED=false OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=https://otlp.example.com OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL=http/protobuf # or grpc Optional settings: per-signal endpoints (OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT, …_METRICS_ENDPOINT, …_LOGS_ENDPOINT; HTTP URLs include /v1/traces, /v1/metrics, /v1/logs), exporter headers for authentication (OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS), sampling (OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER, OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER_ARG; the default samples 10% of new traces), resource attributes (OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES). All variables are listed in the configuration reference.

If you would rather have applications send to a local collector that forwards upstream: Set the upstream in .env: COLLECTOR_UPSTREAM_ENDPOINT=https://otlp.example.com COLLECTOR_UPSTREAM_HEADERS={"Authorization":"Bearer <token>"} Point the applications at the collector: OTEL_SDK_DISABLED=false OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://otel-collector:4318 # HTTP # or http://otel-collector:4317 with OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL=grpc Start the profile: docker compose --env-file .env --profile observability up -d Leave the application exporter headers empty when only the collector needs upstream credentials. The collector's ports are private to the Compose network, and its bounded in-memory queue is telemetry buffering, not durable storage.
Each GitHub webhook delivery stores its W3C trace context (without request bodies or authentication headers), so you can follow a delivery from receipt through worker processing.

Check What it tells you GET /healthz on the web service The web container is up. API readiness The API can reach PostgreSQL. Worker health A heartbeat updated every five seconds after a successful PostgreSQL reconcile and queue probe. Compose health checks use these to order startup and to report docker compose ps.
Preflyt does not install a certificate or reverse proxy. For production, run your own HTTPS proxy in front of the web service.

The web service listens on 127.0.0.1:8080 (or PREFLYT_HTTP_PORT). Forward the entire public origin to it. Preflyt serves the app and forwards /api/ to the API on the same origin, so you do not route the API separately. Requirements: The public origin must match WEB_ORIGIN exactly: HTTPS, no trailing slash, no path. Preserve the original Host header. Preflyt's web service passes it through, and sets its own forwarded headers on the inner hop. Production forces secure cookies and requires HTTPS for OIDC endpoints and callbacks. Webhooks from GitHub reach <WEB_ORIGIN>/api/github/webhooks, so the proxy must accept inbound requests from GitHub.
preflyt.example.com { reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:8080 } Caddy obtains and renews the certificate automatically.

server { listen 443 ssl; server_name preflyt.example.com; ssl_certificate /etc/ssl/preflyt/fullchain.pem; ssl_certificate_key /etc/ssl/preflyt/privkey.pem; location / { proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8080; proxy_set_header Host $host; proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for; } } note These are starting points for your own proxy, not shipped configuration. Review header, body-size and timeout settings for your environment. Webhook bodies are limited to 1 MiB.
Preflyt's web access logs omit query strings, because they can contain OAuth codes and setup state. If your own proxy logs requests, avoid recording full query strings on /api/ paths.

After the proxy is up: Open <WEB_ORIGIN> over HTTPS and confirm the sign-in page loads without mixed-content warnings. Sign in at <WEB_ORIGIN>/super-admin/login. In GitHub, open your App's Advanced tab and redeliver a recent webhook. You should see a 202.

docker compose --env-file .env ps docker compose --env-file .env logs --tail=100 migrate api worker cache queue web Do not share resolved configuration docker compose config and container environment dumps contain resolved secrets. Do not paste them into tickets or chats.

Symptom Likely cause What to do Set POSTGRES_PASSWORD in root .env (or DATABASE_APP_PASSWORD, WEB_ORIGIN, CONFIGURATION_ENCRYPTION_KEY) A required value is missing. Set it in .env and run up again. See Docker Compose. migrate exits with an error A migration failed. The API and web will not start. Read the migrate logs. Keep the volume and your backup. Do not reset the database. api restarts at boot Invalid or partial OIDC configuration, failed issuer discovery, or a configuration decryption error. Provide all OIDC fields or none. Check CONFIGURATION_ENCRYPTION_KEY is the original key. worker stays unhealthy It waits for the API's initial configuration import. Fix the API first, then check the worker. Changing .env passwords has no effect Credentials only initialize roles on a fresh volume. Plan a database-role change. See Upgrades and backups.

Symptom What to check You can't reach /super-admin/login SUPER_ADMIN_USERNAME and SUPER_ADMIN_PASSWORD were both set before first start, and the password is 24 to 128 characters. "Sign-in failed" Wrong username or password. The login is rate-limited, so wait before retrying. "Sign-in expired. Start again." The sign-in attempt timed out. Start from the sign-in page again. You're signed out unexpectedly Super Admin sessions last 24 hours and other sessions eight. Activity does not extend them. Login loops locally Use the same hostname throughout. localhost and 127.0.0.1 have separate cookies. For a local trial on plain http://localhost, set PREFLYT_NODE_ENV=development and PREFLYT_COOKIE_SECURE=false in .env, as in the Quick Start, then run docker compose up -d. Reconnect to Preflyt appears The browser can't confirm your session, usually during an API outage. Use Retry connection. Preflyt does not log you out for transient errors.

Symptom What to check The install redirect fails The App's Setup URL and callback URLs match WEB_ORIGIN exactly, and "Request user authorization during installation" is off. GitHub sign-in is not offered The sign-in switch is on in Settings, GITHUB_USER_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY is set, the login callback is registered, and the saved GitHub connection has refreshed. Deployment encryption-key changes require recreating the affected services. Repositories are missing The App is installed on that organization and has access to the repository. No events appear Event ingestion is on in Settings, the webhook URL is <WEB_ORIGIN>/api/github/webhooks, and the App is subscribed to Pull request, Check run and Workflow run. GitHub can't reach localhost. A delivery returns 401 The webhook secret differs between GitHub and Preflyt. A delivery returns 503 Event ingestion is off or not configured. A delivery shows Processing failed The worker gave up after five attempts. Fix the cause, then an administrator can move that delivery's state in PostgreSQL from FAILED back to RECEIVED and clear its reason and processedAt. There is no button for this yet. A delivery shows Not processed Repository access changed before the worker processed it.

Saved GitHub and governance connections refresh without a restart, as do feature switches. OIDC and SMTP connection changes still require restarting both the API and worker. If a switch suddenly turns off by itself, check the API logs for a configuration read or decryption error. When that happens Preflyt disables live switches rather than falling back to old values.
documents.s: Settings changes do not take effect

documents.t: Email needs SMTP configured in Settings → Configuration by Super Admin. SMTP_ALLOW_INSECURE_LOCAL only helps with a loopback test server in development and is ignored in production.
Collect the service logs above (without secrets) and the exact time of the problem, and open an issue in the Preflyt repository.
This page covers a single-instance Docker Compose installation. Plan upgrades as a short maintenance window.

Two small scripts do the safe thing for you. Download them into the folder that holds compose.yaml and .env: cd /opt/preflyt curl -fsSLO https://lyrisoft.github.io/preflyt/downloads/backup.sh curl -fsSLO https://lyrisoft.github.io/preflyt/downloads/restore.sh chmod +x backup.sh restore.sh

The backup script writes a custom-format PostgreSQL snapshot with private permissions and refuses to overwrite an existing file. ./backup.sh backups/before-upgrade.dump It runs against the db service of the installation in the current folder. The database name defaults to preflyt. Pass another name as a second argument if you changed it. Protect your backups Backups contain sensitive application records and are not encrypted. Store them outside the server with appropriate access control. Also back up your encryption keys separately, because without CONFIGURATION_ENCRYPTION_KEY the saved credentials in a restored database cannot be decrypted.

Restore never touches your original database. It always creates a new database named preflyt_restore_..., restores in one transaction and grants the runtime role access. It fails if that name already exists. Use a fresh name for each attempt. ./restore.sh backups/before-upgrade.dump preflyt_restore_rehearsal Before you rely on a backup, check the restored database for identities, repository selections, audit records and migration history.

To switch to a restored database: Stop web, api and worker: docker compose stop web api worker. Restore into a new database as above. Add PREFLYT_DATABASE=preflyt_restore_<name> to .env. Start Preflyt: docker compose up -d --wait. Keep the original database and the backup until recovery is verified. A restore returns data to the snapshot time. Later writes are not in it.

Record the running PREFLYT_VERSION and the database name. Keep the old images on the server. Check with Lyrisoft whether the new release changes the database in a way that stops the old version from running against it. Stop the application and back up. Change PREFLYT_VERSION in .env to the new release. Pull and migrate, and continue only if it succeeds. Start and check health. docker compose stop web api worker ./backup.sh backups/before-upgrade.dump # Edit .env: set PREFLYT_VERSION to the new release docker compose pull docker compose run --rm migrate docker compose up -d --wait docker compose ps Running migrations again is safe: applied migrations are not repeated. PostgreSQL and its volume stay in place throughout. If a migration or startup fails: keep the application stopped, read the logs: docker compose logs migrate api worker, keep both the backup and the volume. Do not edit applied migration files, reset the database, delete the volume or mark a failed migration as successful.

Migrations are never reversed automatically. If the previous release is compatible with the current schema, set PREFLYT_VERSION back to it and run docker compose up -d --wait. If compatibility is uncertain, restore the pre-upgrade backup into a new database, point PREFLYT_DATABASE at it and start the previous release. This keeps the current database for diagnosis and avoids a destructive in-place rollback.

Base images. Image digests for Node, nginx, PostgreSQL, Valkey and the collector are pinned for reproducibility. Applying patch updates is your task. Resource limits. The shipped memory and CPU limits are starting points, not capacity guarantees. Check usage before raising workloads. Webhook inbox growth. Retention of the webhook inbox is operator-managed. Account for it in storage planning and back up PostgreSQL. PostgreSQL credentials. Credentials in .env initialize roles on a fresh volume only. Rotating them needs a planned database-role change coordinated with the API and migration environment.

Development builds retain sha-<full-commit> image tags. Successful pushes to main publish a GitHub release only after the application images and published-image Compose acceptance pass. The first stable version is v0.1.0; later releases increment the patch version of the highest stable vX.Y.Z Git tag. Release candidates do not advance that stable sequence. The API, migration, native controller and web images all receive the same version tag, for example ghcr.io/lyrisoft/preflyt-web:v0.1.0. These tags reference the verified dual architecture manifests already built for that commit; release creation does not rebuild images. SHA tags remain available for traceability. Retries reuse the version reserved for the commit and refuse to overwrite a version with different image contents. Native scanner images have their own publishing workflow and retain their existing tags. Set PREFLYT_VERSION to the chosen stable version when upgrading. A release publishes images; it does not automatically deploy them to your server. Major and minor version changes require an intentional new stable version tag; ordinary successful main builds increment the patch version automatically.
This guide covers everything you do in Preflyt after it is installed and connected to GitHub. If you have not done that yet, start with Getting Started.

A standard is a versioned set of checks, such as "tests pass" or "no secrets in the code". A policy says which standards a branch must meet, for example main. Your GitHub Actions workflow runs the checks. Preflyt gives you the YAML to add. Each pull request produces a report: what passed, what failed and what has no result yet. Preflyt publishes the result on the pull request as a check. Merge Protection makes GitHub require that check before a merge. You can stop at any step. Reports and checks are useful on their own, and nothing blocks a merge until you require the check in GitHub.

Role What they typically do Super Admin Configures the deployment: GitHub App, sign-in, email, feature switches. Owner and Admin Select repositories, create standards, assign them to teams, manage access. Policy Manager Creates, reviews and publishes policies. Engineering Lead and Developer Create reports and read results for their repositories. Auditor and Viewer Read results. They cannot change anything. See Access Control for the full list.

I want to… Page Create or choose what my code must meet Standards Decide which standards apply to a branch Policies Get checks running on every pull request Pull request checks Make GitHub block a failing pull request Merge Protection See issues across my repositories Findings Apply standards to a group of repositories Teams Invite people and set what they can do Access Control Get AI review comments on pull requests AI reviews Understand optional Preflyt-hosted checks Native execution Review workspace audit history Audit log Get alerts about results Notifications See who works on what Contributors

Access Control decides who can use your workspace and what they can do. Open Administration → Access Control. It has four tabs: People, GitHub members, Roles & permissions and Activity. Only an Owner or Admin can manage people. Everyone else can read the roles.

Role What they can do Owner Manage organization settings, people, repositories and policies. Admin Manage people, repositories and policies. Owner assignment is restricted. Policy Manager Create, review and publish policies. Read assessments and contributor evidence. Security Engineer Review security evidence, manage imported reports and read policies. Engineering Lead Run and review assessments, read policies and contributor evidence. Developer Run assessments and review results for assigned repositories. Auditor Read audit history, assessments, policies and contributor evidence. No changes. Viewer Read repositories, assessments, policies and contributor lists. No changes. Owners and Admins can see every repository in the workspace. All other roles only see the repositories you assign them. The Roles & permissions tab lists exactly what each role can do.

If your workspace is linked to GitHub: Open Access Control and the GitHub members tab. It lists your GitHub organization's members. Use Sync members to refresh it. Select Assign role next to a person, or use Give access and pick someone from the searchable list. People who already have access are not listed. Choose a built-in role and the repositories they should see. Save. Preflyt checks that the person is still an active member of your GitHub organization when you save. The person then signs in with Continue with GitHub. For single sign-on workspaces, use the People tab and Give access with the person's identity from your provider.

You cannot edit your own access. The last active Owner cannot be removed. Only an Owner can assign or change the Owner and Admin roles. Changes take effect on the next request. Removing someone's access stops them straight away.
The Activity tab lists recent access changes: who changed what, and when. For paginated platform activity with action, date and repository filters, use Audit log.

If your workspace already existed before GitHub sign-in, use GitHub members → Link GitHub organization. It verifies the current workspace Owner and a GitHub organization owner before confirming. It keeps your repositories, policies and history. Accounts are never matched by email or username.
documents.s: Link an existing workspace to GitHub

documents.t: AI reviews are optional and advisory. An AI review can explain a failure or comment on changed code, but it never decides whether a pull request passes. Preflyt's checks and policy decide that. You control three things: the model that is used, the skills (instructions) it follows, and whether your code is sent to it.

A deployment administrator must enable AI model configuration and Advisory AI reviews in Settings → Configuration → Intelligence, and set the AI_PROVIDER_ENCRYPTION_KEY key when installing. See Configuration. Until then the AI Intelligence page says AI is disabled for this deployment. Only an Owner or Admin can manage models and routing.

Open AI Intelligence → Models and select Add model. Choose a provider: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, DeepSeek, or an OpenAI-compatible endpoint for a self-hosted model. Enter the exact model name and your API key. Preflyt fills in the provider's endpoint and sign-in details. Save. Saving tests and approves the model for your organization. The test only checks the connection and does not send any of your code. If the test fails, the model is still saved and you can select Test to retry. Keys stay private and are never shown again. Leave the key blank when editing to keep the saved one. No token prices or budgets are required.

Open AI Intelligence → Model router. Configure default picks one model to use everywhere. Stage overrides (optional) let a specific stage use a different primary model and an optional fallback. Leave stages on Use default unless you need this. The Code review model controls the model for reviewing changed code. Here you also decide whether to send repository code to the selected AI model. This is an explicit setting that you control. Preflyt never turns it on for you.

A skill is a short set of review instructions in Markdown, such as "Explain failed checks and missing evidence". Preflyt ships a library of built-in skills. Open Skills: Select Create skill and start from a built-in skill, or choose Upload SKILL.md to load a file. Files must be UTF-8 Markdown up to 32 KiB, with a name and description in the header. Optionally limit the skill to certain repositories. Leave it empty for all repositories you can access. A new skill starts disabled. Review the instructions, source and licence, approve the exact version, then enable it. Editing a skill creates a new version that needs approving again. Skills are attached to a standard: edit the standard, select Add AI Review and pick an approved, enabled skill.

In Settings → PR feedback, turn on Review changed code with AI and comment on PRs. Preflyt then reviews the changed code in each pull request and comments. It also publishes Preflyt / AI Review as an advisory check. AI findings do not override policy results. The integrated final gate waits for configured AI feedback to publish, so a model or publication failure can still fail the workflow. Only actionable changed-code issues are published, with at most five inline comments and deduplication across commits. See Pull request checks.
AI output is kept separate from observed evidence in reports. AI never overrides a failed or incomplete check. AI is optional. Everything else in Preflyt works without it.

Open Administration → Audit log to review recorded workspace actions. Owners, Admins and Auditors can read it within their current workspace and repository permissions. Use the date, action and repository filters, then apply them. Date filters include whole UTC days; table timestamps use your local time and details also show UTC. Results are newest first, 20 per page. The table is paginated; use Previous and Next to review older records. Open an entry for readable actor, action, time and selected details. Filter state is kept in the page URL. Credentials and raw metadata are excluded. Repository access still applies; the log is not an unrestricted view of other workspaces. Background actions may identify a system actor rather than a person. Access Control → Activity remains focused on recent membership and role changes. An audit event records an action, not proof that every related check passed; open its assessment or deployment for the result.

Contributors shows who is working on your repositories, using activity GitHub reports to Preflyt. Open Workspace → Contributors. When a repository is selected, Preflyt reads a limited sample of its recent pull requests, reviews and commits from GitHub. After that, GitHub webhook events keep it current, so the App should be subscribed to Pull request, Pull request review and Push events. See GitHub App. Without webhooks the page shows only that recent sample.

The filters, which are saved in the page address so you can share a link: Repository, or all of them, Period: 7, 30, 90 or 180 days, Kind: human, bot or unknown, Relationship: pull request author, reviewer, commit author, committer or merge actor, Search by GitHub login.
The list shows each contributor with their repositories, pull requests, merges, reviews and commits, and when they were last seen. Select a contributor to open their page.

It has six tabs: Overview, Repositories, Pull requests, Reviews, Policy evidence and Activity. Each pull request and commit links to GitHub, and Policy evidence links to the reports for those commits. A report linked to a commit records that a report exists. It does not mean the commit passed.
Preflyt keeps only minimal records: stable GitHub user IDs, the commit, pull request numbers and timestamps. It does not keep commit messages, review text, email addresses or raw webhook bodies.

Viewers can browse the directory but cannot open detailed contributor activity or policy evidence. Other roles see the repositories they have access to. Use the Help button on the page for definitions and counting rules.
Findings collects the problems your checks reported, across every repository you can see. Open it from Workspace → Findings.

Findings come from saved reports. Each one belongs to a repository and an exact commit: Reported issues: failed checks, plus issues found inside the JUnit and SARIF reports attached to a report. Missing or unverified results: checks that have no usable result yet. Each item links to the report it came from. The list is built from the latest report for each commit. Findings from older commits stay visible but are not labelled "open" or "resolved" for the current branch.

Use the filters at the top: All repositories to narrow to one repository, the severity chart: select a severity to filter by it, All issue statuses to filter by status, Search findings to search by text. The summary shows reported issues, affected repositories, critical and high issues, and evidence gaps.

Open a finding to see its details, then set: Status: Reported, In review or Resolved, Assignee: who is looking at it, Resolution or review note: explain the review or how it was resolved. Choose Save changes. Triage does not change results Your changes apply to that finding at that commit. The report's evidence and the merge review result stay exactly as they were saved. Marking something resolved here does not make a failed check pass.

Pipeline reports arrive through the Action. Older manually imported or unverified evidence is not independent proof that a tool ran. A suppression written in the source report does not waive a policy. Credential-looking text in report messages is left out. If a very large number of reports exist, you see a partial results notice. Narrow the repository filter to see more. If the list is empty, create a report from a repository first. See Your first report.

A pull request check shows a result. Merge Protection is what makes GitHub require it, so a failing or incomplete pull request cannot merge. GitHub is always the one that blocks the merge. Preflyt publishes the result and helps you create the GitHub rule. Open Merge Protection in the sidebar and choose a repository. It has two tabs: Branch rules and PR checks.

The PR checks tab lists the latest check for each pull request: its target branch, whether it was published to GitHub, the current verified Preflyt result and when it last changed. Select a row to open the report, or View on GitHub. A result that is unknown or still pending is never shown with an old passing result. If publishing is off you see a message pointing you to Settings → PR feedback.
You have two options.

In your repository's Settings → Rules (or branch protection), require the status check Preflyt / Engineering Readiness on the branch. GitHub only offers a check by name after it has appeared on at least one pull request, so open one first. Also require your own CI checks as you normally do.
documents.s: Option 1: set the rule yourself in GitHub

documents.t: Under Branch rules, use the three tabs GitHub rulesets, Drafts and Deployments. GitHub rulesets lists the rulesets GitHub already has for the repository, read-only. Drafts → New draft creates a draft ruleset: choose the Target branches from GitHub, choose a Protection profile: Standard (one approval, a pull request, and protection from force pushes and branch deletion), Strict (two approvals, code owner review, approval after the latest push, resolved conversations and up-to-date checks), or Custom protections, review the generated configuration, which includes the required Preflyt / Engineering Readiness check. Saving a draft does not change GitHub. Deployments → Review activation shows the exact GitHub changes and the open pull requests that would be affected. A reviewer approves it, then Activate on GitHub applies it. Preflyt verifies the result. Roll back sets the managed ruleset to disabled and verifies the result. It does not delete it. Other GitHub protections stay in effect. Activation blocks pull requests Once active, pull requests without a passing Preflyt check are blocked. Review the affected pull requests before you activate. Activation needs these, all off or unavailable by default: Ruleset activation turned on in Settings → Configuration → Governance by a Super Admin. The selected GitHub App must have Organization administration: Read and write, approved on its installation. The primary App is used by default; a separate governance App is optional and needs the same permission. A current automatically published passing PR check targeting each branch being protected must exist, bound to the current policy. A manually created assessment or a passing check for a different branch is not enough. A different authorized administrator must approve. A Super Admin who proposed it may approve their own, and that is recorded in the audit history. Use Refresh in GitHub rulesets to fetch the current inventory after an external change or deletion; the fetched timestamp tells you when the list was last read. Managed deployments also check for drift. If someone changes their protections in GitHub, Preflyt shows the differences and does not overwrite them. Resolve drift before rollback. Preflyt does not offer deletion of arbitrary GitHub rulesets; manage those in GitHub.
documents.s: Option 2: let Preflyt manage the ruleset

documents.t: Publish a policy and get your pull request checks passing on a test branch. Open a few real pull requests and confirm the results are right. Then require the check, starting with one repository.
Pull requests from forks and merge queues are not supported. Ruleset management applies to one repository at a time.

Native execution means Preflyt schedules a check in a separate isolated runtime, rather than your GitHub Actions runner running it. It is optional and disabled by default. Use GitHub Actions for normal onboarding; installing Preflyt does not automatically run repository code.

Path Who runs the code What you set up GitHub Actions Your GitHub runner A branch policy, the public Preflyt Action and its final gate in your workflow, plus a reachable API Native execution A separately reviewed Docker or Kubernetes execution controller Dedicated isolated runtime, independent signed runtime review, reviewed tool images, controller credentials, preflight and execution enablement Native execution is implemented and fixture-tested, but production acceptance is incomplete: broad analyzer coverage, independently validated effective isolation and production Kubernetes acceptance remain outstanding. A passing local fixture or Check sandbox response does not establish these. It is not a production-ready replacement for your full CI suite.

The normal stack needs preflyt-api (also used by the worker), preflyt-api-migration and preflyt-web, plus PostgreSQL and Valkey. These application images are currently private; obtain package access and registry credentials as described in Docker Compose. Native execution additionally needs preflyt-native-controller and only the reviewed tools your plan uses: Node, Gitleaks, Semgrep or Trivy. The offline Trivy image bundles vulnerability data. Tool images are pinned by immutable digest and reviewed separately; do not substitute a moving tag. The controller and tool images are not required for GitHub Actions integration. The API and worker have no Docker engine or Kubernetes scheduling credentials. The controller must target a dedicated reviewed runtime, never the application host's Docker socket. Normal Docker Compose startup does not deploy an execution controller.

Native onboarding is an advanced operator task, not a single enable switch: Prepare a dedicated Docker runtime or Kubernetes sandbox with supported strong isolation, denied network access, bounded resources and credential-free jobs. Obtain an independent review and negative-test evidence for escape, metadata access, exfiltration, cross-repository access, resource abuse and cancellation. Install the trusted reviewer public keys and exact signed runtime approval; the review expires within 30 days. Deploy the separate controller with its own signing identity, private journal/state, authenticated HTTPS endpoint and API credential. Keep the independent review signing key outside Preflyt. Review each fixed tool image, configuration, version, licence, scope and expiry. Dependency scanning needs compatible offline vulnerability data no more than 24 hours old. Configure the deployment's native trust settings and enable Native runtime preflight in Settings → Configuration → Native execution. Confirm the live sandbox matches its review. Enable Native execution only after runtime/tool review and acceptance; the controller must also have execution enabled. Recreate services after environment changes; restart API and worker services after OIDC or SMTP connection changes. Saved GitHub connections refresh automatically. Re-check after runtime, image or review changes. A revoked, expired or changed review blocks requests rather than falling back to a weaker runtime. The operator runbook and runner deployment files contain the exact signed schemas, Docker/Kubernetes overrides and credential contracts. These source links require access to the private Preflyt repository. Arrange that access with Lyrisoft before attempting native setup; this page is not a complete standalone production installer.

Select and inspect the repository, and save its standards. Native requests use the recorded commit and selection, not an arbitrary branch tip. Open Assessments → Commit assessments → Execution environment and choose Check sandbox. This checks setup, not the repository's engineering checks. Open View check plan. Review the commit, supported checks, tool review and unavailable adapters. With repository execution.run permission, select supported checks and choose Request checks. Read any blocked reason before retrying. Follow the paginated Check requests history. Cancel request requests cancellation; wait for cleanup confirmation. A request being queued or completed is not a policy pass. Open the saved assessment to see verified results and coverage. Native evidence does not automatically activate GitHub protection or waive missing CI requirements.

Check Fixed adapter Coverage Secret scanning Gitleaks directory scan Reviewed full-rule evidence can be accepted Tests Node built-in test runner Partial; does not run arbitrary project scripts or install dependencies SAST Semgrep with image-owned local rules Partial Lint Narrow image-owned Semgrep lint rules Partial; not the project's full lint configuration Dependency vulnerabilities Trivy with reviewed offline data Partial Infrastructure policy Offline Trivy Terraform/Kubernetes checks Partial Build, type checking, coverage, container-image scanning and exposure adapters are not available in the native controller. Supported adapters use fixed commands; repository or AI-supplied commands are not accepted. Jobs have no dependency-download egress, a five-minute deadline and bounded resources/reports. Kubernetes source bundles over 512 KiB remain incomplete. Verified failures can fail required checks. Clean partial coverage stays incomplete, so keep verified CI evidence for full project checks. Existing CI evidence stays available when native execution is disabled, blocked or unavailable.

Disable execution to stop admission of new requests. Preserve journals and wait for cancellation/cleanup reconciliation before stopping an active controller. Disable preflight and remove the dedicated controller when it is no longer needed. This does not remove your assessments or change GitHub branch protections.
Preflyt can tell you when something needs attention: a new report, a failed result, a published policy and similar events.

Select the bell at the top of any page, or open Notifications. Filter by repository, unread, severity, event type and date. Select Mark all read, or mark items one by one. Notifications only show repositories you can currently access. Losing access hides earlier ones. Notifications are saved assessment updates. They do not confirm that a pull request is ready to merge. If you see Notifications are disabled for this deployment, a Super Admin must turn on Workspace notifications in Settings → Configuration → Notifications.

Owners and Admins, repository-assigned Engineering Leads, the person who created the report, and the linked GitHub author of a pull request can receive assessment alerts. Each needs access to the report. Owners, Admins and Policy Managers receive policy publication notices. Security Engineers with access also receive critical finding and native failure notices.

Open Settings → Notifications (or use the switch in the inbox) to turn your assessment alerts on or off. This affects future alerts only. Muting them does not hide governance, critical finding or AI administration notices.

Email is sent only after a Super Admin sets it up, and each person opts in. Set up delivery (Super Admin): in Settings → Configuration → Notifications, turn on Email notifications and enter the SMTP host, SMTP port, Sender email, SMTP username and SMTP password. Restart the API and worker after changing SMTP. Shared email channels (Owner or Admin): in Settings → Notifications, select Add email channel. Name it, for example Engineering alerts. Enter up to 20 recipient addresses, separated by commas or new lines. Save, then use Send test to check delivery. A channel's recipients are separate from anyone's sign-in email and from personal preferences. If delivery fails, the page says Email delivery is not ready and tells you who to ask.
A policy says which standards a branch must meet. Once published, Preflyt evaluates every pull request into that branch against it. Open Policies in the sidebar.

At the top of the page, Policy scope sets what you are working on: Repository: policies for one repository. Team: assign standards to every repository a team covers. Organization: assign standards to every selected repository. Select Set organization scope to prepare it. Below the scope are two tabs: Branch policies: the policies themselves. CI jobs: connecting your GitHub Actions workflow. See Pull request checks.

Choose Branch policies, then New policy. Enter the Branch name, the branch pull requests target, such as main. Choose the standards the branch must meet, and the Requirement level. Optionally use Make additional checks required to turn optional checks into required ones. Create the draft. Organization and team requirements are included automatically. A repository policy can add to them but not weaken them.

A new policy is a draft. To use it: Review the draft. You see the saved standard versions, inherited team standards and any AI Reviews, which are suggestions only. Approve it. Approval needs a different authorized reviewer than the person who created it. A Super Admin can approve their own draft, and that exception is recorded in the audit history. Publish it. Publishing lets Preflyt evaluate pull requests against the approved policy. It saves a non-blocking policy: it does not activate any GitHub rule. To make GitHub enforce it, see Merge Protection. If the saved standards change after you create a draft, Preflyt tells you to edit the draft or create a new version before approval. Published policies are never altered. To use newer standards, create a new revision.
Review the check sources and create a fresh report before you ask for merge protection. Publishing does not mean every check passed: results come from your pull requests.

Preflyt can check every pull request against your published policy and show the result on the pull request as a GitHub check named Preflyt / Engineering Readiness. Your own GitHub Actions workflow runs the tests and scanners. Preflyt then verifies that the run really happened and evaluates the result.

A result only counts when Preflyt verifies the actual report-producing jobs for the current run attempt and PR head commit. The final gate runs in the same workflow after those jobs finish; Preflyt does not wait for that gate to finish before evaluating its predecessors. An uploaded report or a success label on its own can never produce a pass.

Check each of these. Several need a deployment administrator. # What Where 1 The GitHub App has Checks: Read and write, Actions: Read-only and Pull requests: Read (write for comments). GitHub App 2 The repository is selected. Repositories 3 Public Preflyt API URL is set to a public HTTPS address that GitHub can reach, not localhost. With Preflyt's bundled web proxy, include /api, for example https://preflyt.example.com/api. Settings → Configuration → GitHub (Super Admin) 4 Publish PR checks and Automatic PR checks are on. Settings → Configuration → Governance (Super Admin) 5 A policy is published for the branch pull requests target. Policies 6 PR checks are on for the repository. Settings → PR feedback For item 6, open Settings → PR feedback, choose the repository and select Enable checks. Enable checks for all turns them on for every connected repository. The Public Preflyt API URL applies without a restart. If it is empty, the snippet shows <PUBLIC_PREFLYT_API_URL> and a note tells you to ask a deployment administrator to set it.

Open Policies and choose the CI jobs tab. Choose the repository and the branch policy. Under Policy workflow snippet, select Copy snippet. You can also use View YAML on any standard in Standards. Paste it into your pull request workflow, for example .github/workflows/ci.yml. Keep your own dependency installation steps before the Preflyt step. Commit it to a branch and open a pull request. The generated standalone snippet has two jobs. When integrating with an existing workflow, keep its check jobs and add one terminal gate: preflyt_checks runs your checks and submits the results using the Preflyt Action. preflyt_gate (named Preflyt final gate) waits for Preflyt's verified result and fails if the policy fails or is incomplete. It depends on every other job in that PR workflow. Do not add a separate workflow_run publication-gate workflow. Documentation and post-merge deployment workflows can remain separate. The snippet already contains your API URL, a pinned release of the Preflyt Action and the check IDs of your policy, so copy it from Preflyt rather than writing it by hand. # Shape of the generated snippet. Copy the real one from Preflyt. jobs: preflyt_checks: runs-on: ubuntu-latest permissions: contents: read id-token: write # lets the Action prove its identity to Preflyt steps: - uses: actions/checkout@... with: ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }} persist-credentials: false # Your dependency installation steps go here. - name: Preflyt policy if: ${{ always() && github.event_name == 'pull_request' }} uses: lyrisoft/preflyt-action@<pinned commit> with: api-url: https://preflyt.example.com/api checks: | { "tests.required": { "report": ".preflyt/results/tests.required.xml", ... } } preflyt_gate: name: Preflyt final gate needs: [preflyt_checks] # ...
documents.s: Add the checks to your workflow

documents.t: For these check IDs the Action reuses the tools already installed on the runner and does not install anything: tests.required, types.required, build.required, lint.required, security.sast, secrets.scan, security.dependencies, containers.scan, iac.policy and iac.exposures. Tests produce JUnit reports and security checks produce SARIF. For any other check, generate the report in an earlier step, or give the check a Workflow command and Result file when you create it in Standards. The snippet notes any check that still needs one. An Action submission can include up to 10 reports. Custom commands must produce real results for the selected check; missing or unrelated reports cannot satisfy it.

Instead of pasting, open the CI jobs tab and use the GitHub workflow panel: Choose the workflow to change with Choose workflow. Optionally use Edit YAML to adjust it, or Rewrite with AI to merge the checks into an existing workflow. Review the proposal before using it. Choose Create setup PR. Preflyt opens a pull request that adds the workflow. It never edits your default branch directly, and the App needs Contents, Workflows and Pull requests write permission for this. Download files is a fallback if you would rather commit it yourself.
documents.s: Let Preflyt open the pull request for you

documents.t: Where What Checks tab Preflyt / Engineering Readiness: passed, failed or incomplete. Checks tab Preflyt final gate: the job in your workflow that fails when the result is failed or incomplete. Checks tab Preflyt / AI Review, if AI reviews are on. It is always advisory. Pull request comment An optional policy summary, if you turn it on in Settings → PR feedback. Preflyt A report under Assessments, and a row in Merge Protection → PR checks. After the first verified run, Preflyt connects the workflow automatically and shows Workflow connected. Completed runs appear in Assessments. Under Recent policy runs you can open each report.
documents.s: What you see on a pull request

documents.t: In Settings → PR feedback: Post a policy summary comment on the PR adds one comment per pull request. Review changed code with AI and comment on PRs turns on AI review. It needs AI set up. Comments and AI suggestions are feedback. Findings never override the deterministic check result. When automatic AI feedback is enabled, the final gate waits for its publication; a provider or publication failure can fail the workflow even though the AI findings themselves are advisory. Inline feedback is limited to five actionable issues and deduplicated across commits; the PR summary is kept short.

Policies select requirements for the PR target branch. They do not rewrite your workflow triggers or job conditions. To run different checks for development and main, publish a policy for each, then update the workflow with branch conditions and real reports that satisfy each policy. Re-run a PR to each target to verify the routing. PR validation does not inherently require Docker images. Type checks, lint, compilation, tests and scanners can run on the runner. Docker Compose integration tests do need images or prebuilt images, so schedule them explicitly where needed. Building and publishing deployment images belongs in a separate post-merge push workflow when that matches your release process. Preflyt does not deploy your application or publish its images for you.
A check on a pull request does not block anything by itself. To make GitHub require it, see Merge Protection.

Pull requests from the same repository only. Fork pull requests and merge queues are not supported. Draft pull requests are not checked. The runner must be Linux with Python 3 and Git. GitHub's ubuntu-latest has both. The Action must run in a job with contents: read and id-token: write.

Symptom Check The snippet shows <PUBLIC_PREFLYT_API_URL> A deployment administrator has not set Public Preflyt API URL. The Action fails to reach Preflyt The API URL must be public HTTPS. GitHub's runners cannot reach localhost, a private network or a self-signed certificate. No workflows found Commit the snippet to a workflow file in the repository first. No Preflyt / Engineering Readiness check PR checks are off for the repository, Publish PR checks is off, no policy is published for the target branch, or the App lacks Checks: write. The gate job times out Preflyt did not verify the run in time. Open the report and the webhook deliveries.

A standard is a versioned set of checks that your code should meet, for example "Application Security". Preflyt ships five built-in standards, and you can copy them or create your own. Open Standards in the sidebar.

The five built-in standards are Baseline Engineering, Application Security, Backend Services, Frontend Applications and Infrastructure as Code. Each has a version, and a version never changes once published. Select Built-in standards to browse them. Open one to see its checks and which are required at each requirement level.

Select New standard, or copy a built-in standard as a starting point. Choose the checks it includes from the available checks. Use Filter checks to find one. Optionally select Add check to define a custom check: give it a name and a short description of what it covers and how to fix a failure, choose its Result source: Test report (JUnit) or Scan report (SARIF), optionally set a Workflow command: the test or scan command to run. Leave it empty to use the built-in recipe if one exists, optionally set the Result file: where the command writes its report, for example reports/tests.xml. Optionally select Add AI Review to attach an approved skill. AI Reviews only give suggestions. See AI reviews. Save. Your standard appears under Organization standards. If a standard has no checks yet, the page says Create a standard or copy one from Built-in standards.

Saved versions stay unchanged. Editing a standard creates a new version, and the history is kept. A policy keeps using the version it was published with until you publish a new revision of that policy, so editing a standard never changes a published policy by surprise.

Every standard card has View YAML. It shows the GitHub Actions snippet that runs that standard's checks. Use Copy snippet to copy it. Individual checks have snippets too. See Pull request checks for where it goes.
documents.s: Use a standard in a workflow

documents.t: Each repository has its own selection: Open the repository and select the Standards tab. Choose Choose standards. Pick a Requirement level: Core: baseline requirements. Recommended: adds broader checks. Strict: also requires resilience checks. Choose up to five standards. Those that match the repository's detected stack are marked Recommended. Review the changes Preflyt shows, then choose Save standards. Saving standards does not turn on GitHub merge protection, and existing policies keep their approved version. To enforce standards on a branch, create a policy. Only an Owner or Admin can change a repository's standards.

A team groups people and the repositories they own, so you can apply the same standards to all of them at once. Open Administration → Teams. Teams organize people and requirements. They never grant access to Preflyt or GitHub.

You can: select Create team and choose existing workspace members, or select Import from GitHub to bring in a team from your connected GitHub organization. Imports are read-only and start with no repositories in scope. The App needs Members: Read-only for this. Each team has tabs: Overview, Members, Repositories, Standards & policies, Effective impact and Activity.

In the team's Repositories tab, review the repositories and explicitly approve the ones whose policies the team may set. Only repositories you are allowed to manage and that are selected in Preflyt are offered. A team can include child teams. Select Preview scope to see the exact list of repositories that would be added, then Approve scope. This records the approval. It does not give anyone access, change an existing policy or activate any GitHub rule.
documents.s: Choose which repositories a team covers

documents.t: Open Policies and choose Team as the policy scope, then pick the team. You can also use the team's Standards & policies tab. Choose the exact standard versions, a requirement level and the branch. Preview the checks added to each repository, and any conflicts. Apply the preview. This creates a standards selection and a policy draft for each repository. Review each draft, then approve and publish it in Policies. A different authorized reviewer must approve. If anything changes while you are previewing, preview again before applying. Effective impact shows each repository's policy status. A published policy does not mean every check passed.

Use Organization-wide requirements (the Organization baseline) to apply one shared set of standards to every selected repository. A repository cannot weaken or bypass a baseline. A new repository needs explicit approval and re-applying before it is covered.

In Standards & policies, choose Upgrade next to an active assignment, pick the new versions, preview and apply. The old assignment is kept for history and new drafts are created. Already published policies are never changed until you publish a new revision.

500 teams per organization. 100 members and 100 repositories per team. 100 assignments per team. At most five standards combined. You cannot remove a repository from a team while the team has an active standards assignment covering it.
